title: Focus & Pomodoro
examples: How long should my focus blocks be?
What is the best way to use my breaks?
What are the biggest distractions when I study?

explain.say: Today we are learning about focus blocks for studying.

draw.text: Focus Blocks: Short bursts of work

explain.say: A good focus block means working without stopping.
After a focus block, you need a planned break time.

draw.text: Breaks: Rest your mind and body

explain.say: Breaks should let your brain rest from the task.
Removing distractions helps you keep your focus strong.

draw.text: Distractions: Keep them out of sight

explain.say: In real life, you use this when studying for a big test.

faq.q: How long should my focus blocks be for best results?
faq.a: Many people find 25 minutes to be a good starting point for a focus block. You can adjust this time as you get more practiced.
asks: What is the right time for deep work?
Should I study for an hour straight?

faq.q: What counts as a good break?
faq.a: A good break means doing something completely different from studying. Moving your body or looking out a window works well.
asks: Can I just scroll on my phone during a break?
What should I do when I take a break?

faq.q: Why is it hard to remove distractions?
faq.a: Our brains are naturally drawn to novelty, so things like phones seem very interesting. You must actively put away the things that pull your attention.
asks: Why do I keep checking my phone?
How do I ignore my phone while studying?

faq.q: Does the Pomodoro Technique work for all subjects?
faq.a: Yes, this technique is useful for almost any subject because it trains your brain to work in manageable chunks. It helps build stamina.
asks: Is this only for reading books?
Can I use this for maths problems too?

faq.q: What if I feel too tired to focus?
faq.a: If you feel very tired, take a longer break than usual. Sometimes a quick snack or a few deep breaths can help reset your focus.
asks: When should I take a longer break?
What if I feel burnt out?

facts: A focus block is a dedicated period for deep, uninterrupted work.
Short breaks help prevent mental fatigue and improve concentration.
Identifying distractions is the first step to removing them from your study area.
The Pomodoro Technique suggests using a timer to structure work and rest.

quiz.say: If you study for 25 minutes, what should you do next?

options.show: Check your phone for five minutes
options.say: Check your phone for five minutes

options.show: Take a long break of an hour
options.say: Take a long break of an hour

quiz.why: This follows the pattern of focused work followed by rest.

wrong.0: This leads to burnout because your brain needs time to rest.
wrong.1: This is a distraction, not a true rest for your mind.
wrong.2: A very long break might make it hard to start studying again later.

quiz.say: Which action best represents removing a distraction?
quiz.show: Distraction: Phone visible vs. Phone away

options.show: Putting your phone in another room
options.say: Putting your phone in another room

quiz.why: Physical distance helps your brain ignore the temptation.

wrong.0: It is still visible and might tempt you to check it.
wrong.1: While good, this does not remove the temptation to pick it up.
wrong.2: Music can sometimes be a distraction itself, depending on the song.

quiz.say: If your focus block is 25 minutes, and your break is 5 minutes, how many cycles complete one full session?
quiz.why: One full cycle includes both the work period and the rest period.

wrong.0: This would mean working for 50 minutes straight.
wrong.1: You must complete at least one full work/break cycle.
wrong.2: While subjects matter, the structure of the cycle remains the same.
